items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: He said, this man scores all my wife's pictures, Alice Faye, you know.

ctx.x: Anyway -- I think it's back on the other page, Mel. Anyway, when I was writing for Tony Paster, we were -- I went up -- we were in the Paramount theater here in New York, and so I said, after -- well, I wasn't playing in the band, but I had to be there every day because I'm the arranger, you know, and sometimes we'd rehearse between shows. So after one of the shows, I went to Tony Paster's room. I used to go into his dressing room all the time and talk to him. When I went into the room, there was Phil Harris.…

pretty cool cat. So I mean he wanted -- probably had something to say to me, and he said, do you know Benny Carter? I say, oh, sure. I said, I know Benny Carter very well, he's a good friend of mine. He says, let me tell you something. He said, I didn't know he was the kind of musician that he is. I say, oh, I thought everybody knew Benny Carter was a musician. He said, this man scores all my wife's pictures, Alice Faye, you know. He said, he's just finished scoring a picture, and he says that when the cats can't…
Beautiful. Now you mentioned something about Bird -- Charlie Parker.
